# `facility-registry`

Interface reference generated from the contract spec embedded in `facility_registry.wasm`. See the contract's hand-written docs for design context.

## Functions

### `accept_admin`

```rust
fn accept_admin() -> Result<(), Error>
```

Accept the proposed admin transfer. The caller must authorize as the pending admin.

### `add_affiliation_period`

```rust
fn add_affiliation_period(facility: FacilityId, attester: Address, from: u64, to: Option<u64>) -> Result<(), Error>
```

Record that `attester` was affiliated with `facility` over `[from, to)`.
Requires the admin's authorization.

Periods are stored in fixed-size pages (`AffiliationPage(facility, attester, page_no)`)
so no single storage entry grows without bound; the latest period is also
mirrored into a small header for O(1) `is_affiliated`. Returns
`Error::AffiliationPeriodOverlap` if the new period overlaps an existing one.

### `deactivate_facility`

```rust
fn deactivate_facility(facility: FacilityId, reason: DeactivationReason, at: u64) -> Result<(), Error>
```

Deactivate `facility` at ledger timestamp `at`, recording a
`DeactivationReason` (`Closed`, `LicenceLapsed`, or `Fraud`). Requires the
admin's authorization. Emits `FacilityDeactivated` with the reason and
timestamp.

Attestations made **before** `at` remain valid, except when the reason is
`Fraud`: those are reported as `facility_untrusted` from `at` onwards,
mirroring attester compromise windows. See `verify_attestation`.

### `get_affiliation_periods`

```rust
fn get_affiliation_periods(facility: FacilityId, attester: Address, cursor: u32, limit: u32) -> AffiliationPeriodPage
```

Return one page of the affiliation history for `(facility, attester)`,
ordered by start time. `cursor` is the page number to start from (use `0`
for the first page); `limit` is capped at `AFFILIATION_PAGE_LIMIT`. The
returned `AffiliationPeriodPage` carries the periods and the `next_cursor`
(`None` when the history is exhausted). Callers must not assume the whole
history fits in one response.

```rust
fn get_deactivation(facility: FacilityId) -> Option<Deactivation>
```

Return the recorded deactivation (reason and timestamp) for `facility`, or
`None` if the facility is active.

### `reactivate_facility`

```rust
fn reactivate_facility(facility: FacilityId) -> Result<(), Error>
```

Reactivate a previously deactivated facility. Requires the admin's
authorization. Emits `FacilityReactivated`. Past deactivations remain in
the event log; the current deactivation record is cleared.

### `register_facility`

```rust
fn register_facility(id: FacilityId, code_hash: BytesN<32>, local_alias: Option<u64>) -> Result<(), Error>
```

Enroll a facility under its portable `FacilityId` (see
`docs/specs/facility-id.md`), indexing it by `code_hash` for lookup via
`get_facility_by_code`. `local_alias` optionally records the legacy
sequential `u64` ID so existing consumers keep working during migration.
Requires the admin's authorization.

### `was_affiliated_at`

```rust
fn was_affiliated_at(facility: FacilityId, attester: Address, at: u64) -> bool
```

Whether `attester` was affiliated with `facility` at ledger timestamp `at`.
Binary-searches the fixed-size affiliation pages, so the read cost is
O(log n) storage entries in the number of periods.

## Types

### `AffiliationPeriod`

A half-open affiliation interval `[from, to)`; `to == None` means ongoing.

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `from` | `u64` | Start ledger timestamp (inclusive). |
| `to` | `Option<u64>` | End ledger timestamp (exclusive), or `None` while ongoing. |

### `AffiliationPeriodPage`

One page of paginated affiliation history.

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `periods` | `Vec<AffiliationPeriod>` | The periods in this page, ordered by start time. |
| `next_cursor` | `Option<u32>` | Cursor to pass to the next `get_affiliation_periods` call, or `None` if exhausted. |

### `Deactivation`

The recorded deactivation of a facility.

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `reason` | `DeactivationReason` | Why the facility was deactivated. |
| `at` | `u64` | Ledger timestamp at which the deactivation took effect. |

### `DeactivationReason`

Why a facility was deactivated.

| Variant | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `Closed` | The facility closed. Prior attestations remain valid. |
| `LicenceLapsed` | The facility's licence lapsed. Prior attestations remain valid. |
| `Fraud` | The facility is untrusted. Attestations made before deactivation are reported as `facility_untrusted`. |

### `Facility`

An enrolled facility record.

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `FacilityId` | The portable facility identifier. |
| `code_hash` | `BytesN<32>` | Hash of the canonical external facility code. |
| `local_alias` | `Option<u64>` | Legacy sequential ID, if recorded during migration. |

### `FacilityId`

A portable facility identifier: `BytesN<32>` computed as
`H(domain || jurisdiction || issuing_authority || facility_code)`. Unlike
the legacy sequential `u64`, it is stable across re-genesis, multiple
jurisdictions, and federation. See `docs/specs/facility-id.md` for the
canonicalization rules and test vectors.

## Errors (`Error`)

| Code | Name | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `NotInitialized` | `initialize` has not been called yet. |
| 2 | `AlreadyInitialized` | `initialize` was called more than once. |
| 3 | `NoPendingTransfer` | `accept_admin` was called with no pending admin transfer. |
| 4 | `FacilityNotFound` | The referenced facility is not enrolled. |
| 5 | `FacilityAlreadyExists` | A facility with this `FacilityId` or external code hash is already enrolled. |
| 6 | `AffiliationPeriodOverlap` | The new affiliation period overlaps an existing period for the same `(facility, attester)`. |
| 7 | `InvalidPeriod` | The affiliation period is malformed (e.g. `to <= from`). |
| 8 | `MigrationNotRequired` | `migrate()` was called while the stored schema version is already `>= SCHEMA_VERSION`. |

### `accept_admin`


### `add_attester`

```rust
fn add_attester(attester: Address) -> Result<(), Error>
```

Add `attester` to the allowlist. Requires the admin's authorization.
Fails with `Error::AllowlistFull` if the allowlist is at capacity and
`attester` is not already present (see `set_max_attesters`).

### `add_attester_with_info`

```rust
fn add_attester_with_info(attester: Address, license_hash: Option<BytesN<32>>, region: Option<Symbol>) -> Result<(), Error>
```

Add `attester` with optional metadata to the allowlist. Requires the admin's authorization.
Fails with `Error::AllowlistFull` if the allowlist is at capacity and
`attester` is not already present (see `set_max_attesters`).

### `add_attesters`

```rust
fn add_attesters(attesters: Vec<Address>) -> Result<(), Error>
```

Add multiple attesters to the allowlist in a single transaction.

Requires the admin's authorization. Blocked while the contract is paused.
Returns `Error::BatchTooLarge` if `attesters.len() > BATCH_LIMIT`.
Returns `Error::AllowlistFull` if adding the new (non-duplicate)
addresses would exceed the configured `max_attesters` cap. Addresses
that are already allowlisted are silently skipped (idempotent), so the
call never fails due to duplicates in the batch and no duplicate events
are emitted. Exactly one `AttesterAdded` event is emitted per newly
added address.

### `migrate`

```rust
fn migrate() -> Result<(), Error>
```

Run any pending storage migration, then record the new schema
version. Requires the admin's authorization.

Call this after `upgrade()` only when the new build bumps
`SCHEMA_VERSION` (a storage-schema-changing release) \xe2\x80\x94 including the
first upgrade of a legacy (pre-versioning, schema version `0`)
instance, which must be migrated to version 1. When no migration is
pending (`SchemaVersion >= SCHEMA_VERSION`) this returns
`Error::MigrationNotRequired` so the call can't accidentally re-run.

### `pause`

```rust
fn pause() -> Result<(), Error>
```

Pause the contract, blocking `add_attester`, `add_attester_with_info`,
`update_attester_info`, `remove_attester`, `suspend_attester`, and
`reinstate_attester` until `unpause` is called. Requires the admin's
authorization.

### `propose_admin`

```rust
fn propose_admin(new_admin: Address) -> Result<(), Error>
```

Propose a new admin address. The caller must authorize as the current admin.
Calling this a second time before `accept_admin` overwrites any pending proposal \xe2\x80\x94 the most recent call wins.

### `reinstate_attester`

```rust

```

Reinstate a suspended attester. Requires the admin's authorization.

### `remove_attester`

```rust
fn remove_attester(attester: Address) -> Result<(), Error>
```

Remove `attester` from the allowlist. Requires the admin's
authorization. A no-op if the attester was never allowlisted.

### `remove_attesters`

```rust
fn remove_attesters(attesters: Vec<Address>) -> Result<(), Error>
```

Remove multiple attesters from the allowlist in a single transaction.

Requires the admin's authorization. Blocked while the contract is paused.
Returns `Error::BatchTooLarge` if `attesters.len() > BATCH_LIMIT`.
Addresses that are not currently allowlisted are silently skipped
(idempotent), so the call never fails if an address was already removed
and no spurious events are emitted. Exactly one `AttesterRemoved` event
is emitted per address that was actually removed.

### `set_max_attesters`

```rust
fn set_max_attesters(max_attesters: u32) -> Result<(), Error>
```

Set the soft cap on the number of allowlisted attesters. Requires the
admin's authorization. Does not evict existing attesters if lowered
below the current count; it only blocks further `add_attester` calls.

### `suspend_attester`

```rust
fn suspend_attester(attester: Address) -> Result<(), Error>
```

Suspend an allowlisted attester. Requires the admin's authorization.

**Note:** this function does **not** check whether `attester` was ever
added via `add_attester`. If called on an address that is not in the
allowlist, it silently sets the `Suspended` storage key and emits
`AttesterSuspended` for that address \xe2\x80\x94 a no-op from an access-control
perspective because `is_attester` also checks for an `Attester` storage
entry, so the phantom suspension has no effect on allowlist queries.
This diverges from `update_attester_info`, which returns
`Error::AttesterNotFound` for unknown addresses. The inconsistency is
known and documented here rather than silently changed; a follow-up
issue should decide whether to align both functions.

### `unpause`

```rust
fn unpause() -> Result<(), Error>
```

Resume normal operation after a `pause`. Requires the admin's authorization.

### `update_attester_info`

```rust
fn update_attester_info(attester: Address, license_hash: Option<BytesN<32>>, region: Option<Symbol>) -> Result<(), Error>
```

Update the metadata of an already-allowlisted `attester`. Requires
the admin's authorization. Unlike `add_attester_with_info`, this
never enrolls a new attester: it fails with `Error::AttesterNotFound`
if `attester` is not currently allowlisted (never added, or since
removed), and always emits `AttesterInfoUpdated` rather than
`AttesterAdded`, so profile changes are distinguishable from
enrollment.

### `upgrade`

```rust
fn upgrade(new_wasm_hash: BytesN<32>) -> Result<(), Error>
```

Upgrade the contract's Wasm code to a new version.
Requires the admin's authorization.

Runbook:
1. Build the new Wasm binary (e.g. `cargo build --workspace --release --target wasm32v1-none`).
2. Upload/install the new Wasm on-chain to obtain its 32-byte hash (`new_wasm_hash`).
3. The admin calls this `upgrade` function passing the `new_wasm_hash`.

For any accompanying state/data migrations, see the storage-versioning guidelines
(e.g. implementing migration scripts or handling lazy migrations on reading old schema versions).

## Errors (`Error`)

| Code | Name | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `NotInitialized` | `initialize` has not been called yet; call `initialize(admin: Address)` before using the contract. |
| 2 | `AlreadyInitialized` | `initialize` was called more than once. |
| 3 | `NoPendingTransfer` | `accept_admin` was called with no pending admin transfer. Admin transfer is a two-step flow: the current admin must first call `propose_admin` to nominate a successor, then the nominated address must call `accept_admin` to complete the transfer. This error is returned when `accept_admin` is called before a corresponding `propose_admin` call has set a pending admin. |
| 4 | `ContractPaused` | The requested operation is blocked while the contract is paused. |
| 5 | `AllowlistFull` | The allowlist is at its configured maximum size. Raise the cap via `set_max_attesters`, or free a slot via `remove_attester`. |
| 6 | `MigrationNotRequired` | `migrate()` was called while the stored schema version is already `>= SCHEMA_VERSION`. Only call `migrate()` after `upgrade()` to a build that bumps `SCHEMA_VERSION`; this error is a safe no-op signal that there is nothing pending, not a failure to react to. |
| 7 | `AttesterNotFound` | The referenced attester is not currently allowlisted (never added, or since removed). |
| 8 | `BatchTooLarge` | The supplied batch exceeds `BATCH_LIMIT` addresses. |
